intro.title: Build typed pagination hook
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable, typed custom React hook for pagination in TypeScript. You'll learn to manage pagination state—like the current page and items per page—using TypeScript generics to keep your data type-safe. The core concepts involve creating a custom hook with useState and useMemo, and structuring a return object with page data and navigation functions. By the end, you'll have a flexible hook that can paginate any array of items while ensuring full type safety throughout your application.
intro.usecase: Typed pagination hooks are essential for managing large datasets in real-world applications like e-commerce product listings, admin dashboards with user tables, or content-heavy platforms displaying articles or search results. In these scenarios, developers need to handle paginated API responses while maintaining type safety for items, page numbers, and loading states. For example, when building a customer management dashboard, a typed pagination hook ensures that user data, current page, and total count are properly typed, preventing runtime errors and improving developer experience. This pattern also enables consistent pagination behavior across different components, such as data tables, product grids, or comment sections, while leveraging TypeScript's autocomplete and error checking.
